title: The Net Mender
text: An old woman mends nets on a stilt-house over the marsh, humming to herself, her fingers quick. Her nets hang drying all around, full not of fish but of shoes, hands, a doll and a crown. Her nets catch whatever the water takes.

options.label: The one with the sea in them helps her haul, so the water gives up what it holds.

outcomes.text: The net comes up heavy with a drowned knight's gear, though nothing of the knight. She does not seem surprised.

options.label: The one with the hurt arm lets her bind it in net-cord, without asking what she hums.

outcomes.text: The old marsh-craft holds, though she charges for it. Her humming stays in their head for days.

options.label: Cut her nets loose to free whatever the water took.

outcomes.text: Whatever was in them swims free. It remembers you.
